slides.headline:
Seoul lost 492 cafes
in twelve months.
slides.subline: The city's coffee scene is now a reason people fly here. That is not the same thing as a good business

slides.label: Seoul held 27,351 coffee and beverage outlets in the second quarter of 2026, down from 27,843 a year earlier. In that single quarter 1,040 opened and 992 closed — the net loss is small, the churn underneath it is not
slides.note: Source: Seoul Economic Daily, 6 October 2026, citing Seoul's commercial district analysis service · Checked 7 October 2026

slides.title:
A boom that
stopped growing.
slides.body:
Korea went from 45,203 cafes in early 2018 to a peak of 96,080 in early 2024 — then fell to 95,337 by the first quarter of 2025, the first decline since the figures began in 2018. That is roughly one cafe for every 540 people.

Demand was never the problem. Euromonitor figures reported by the Korea Herald put Korean consumption near 405 cups per person a year against a global average of 152. The problem is arithmetic: rent, labour and bean costs rose while the headline americano stayed near 1,500 won, and low barriers to entry keep pulling new operators into the same streets.

items.d: Mega MGC, Compose and Paik's standardised on a cheap americano in a large 600-730ml cup with two shots. Built for takeaway, not for sitting
Tom N Toms charged 4,400 won and reported operating losses four years running from 2020. Mid-tier chains struggle to say what they are for

items.t: Around 5,000 won — the place you stay
items.d: Starbucks held 65.6% brand preference among Koreans aged 20-59 and close to 3 trillion won in annual sales. People buy the room as much as the coffee
Single-origin roasteries price against beans that run $20-30 per 100g, with rare microlots reaching $1,500 per kilo

slides.title:
What this means
if you're visiting

items.t: The 1,500-won cup is not a tourist trap
items.d: It is what most Koreans drink on a weekday. Yellow-signed chains on every block are the normal option, not the lesser one

items.t: Price is the clearest signal of intent
items.d: Under 2,000 won is built for takeaway. Past 6,000 won you are usually paying a roaster for a specific bean

items.t: Micro-roasteries are now a draw in themselves
items.d: Squeezed on price, independents competed on rare beans instead. Forbes wrote in September 2026 that tourists have found Seoul's coffee culture and there is nowhere else like it in Asia

items.t: Go early in a cafe's life
items.d: With 992 closures in one Seoul quarter, a shop you bookmark may not be open next trip. Check before you cross the city for it

slides.text:
A long line is not proof of a good business.
It is often just a long line.
slides.by: The Seoul Economic Daily reported on 6 October 2026 that the rapper Hanhae put his cafe losses at 150 to 200 million won over two years, and that Lee Hyori said of her husband's Jeju cafe that despite queues running hundreds of metres, they did not actually make much money. This post is research, not a personal visit. Every figure here comes from a published source, checked on 7 October 2026.

We check every claim before we post it.
Save this before your next Seoul coffee run

caption:
Seoul had 27,351 coffee and beverage outlets in the second quarter of 2026, against 27,843 a year earlier. A net loss of 492 — but inside that same quarter 1,040 shops opened and 992 closed. The churn is the story, not the net.

The national arc explains it. Korea went from 45,203 cafes in early 2018 to a peak of 96,080 in early 2024, then slipped to 95,337 by Q1 2025 — the first decline since the series began. That is about one cafe for every 540 people, in a country drinking roughly 405 cups per person a year against a global average of 152.

So the market split in two. At one end, Mega MGC, Compose and Paik's sell a large americano near 1,500 won; Mega MGC averaged 412.87m won per store in 2024, which the Asia Business Daily put at around 755 cups a day. At the other end, roasteries price against beans at $20-30 per 100g and sell a cup at 6,500-8,000 won. The middle is where it hurts — Tom N Toms, at 4,400 won, reported operating losses four years running from 2020.

For a visitor that split is useful. Under 2,000 won is a takeaway cup and what most locals actually drink. Past 6,000 won you are paying a roaster for a specific bean — and that end of the market is now a reason people fly in. Forbes wrote in September that tourists have found Seoul's coffee culture and there is nowhere else like it in Asia.

One caveat worth keeping: a queue is not proof of a healthy business. Sources in the last slide.
